title: Lyons-Brown absorber geometry and neutrality-measurement preflight

scope.geometry: Inclusive integer spacetime boxes with an explicit L-infinity distance and causally opened or terminated absorbers.
scope.linking: Deterministic enforcement of the three direct-link restrictions stated in Lyons-Brown Theorem 4.
scope.neutrality: Binary e/m parity observations recorded only for an active, cluster-owned ungauged region and then passed to the abstract schedule state.
not_in_scope: microscopic D(S3) gauging or ungauging circuits
derivation of e/m parities from a circuit-level measurement model
cluster discovery from noisy detector histories
proof or numerical reproduction of the Q >= 60 linking bound
schedule performance, threshold, or fault tolerance

invariants: all geometry uses an explicit equal-dimensional L-infinity metric
only causally active absorbers contribute to nearest-distance queries
an absorber is opened once and terminated once on a monotone clock
a cluster's own absorbing region can be excluded from its nearest-external-absorber query
direct links point from a smaller level to a strictly larger level
a smaller cluster has at most one directly linked larger cluster
an absorbing region has at most one directly linked child at each level
neutrality is measured only in an active ungauged region owned by the schedule cluster
neutrality measurements are current-round records and cannot precede ungauging
the schedule consumes measured parity labels rather than simulation truth

verified_cases: nearest active absorber is selected by box-to-box L-infinity distance and bound into the schedule age gate
terminated absorbers disappear from later nearest-distance queries
a cluster-owned absorbing region can be excluded from an external-distance query
all three direct-link restrictions reject invalid forests
neutral e/m parities update an owned active D(Z3) cluster
non-neutral parity is retained while a terminated region rejects later measurement
future-round and wrong-owner neutrality records are rejected

claim_boundary: This verifies a deterministic source-level geometry and measurement interface. It does not implement microscopic D(S3) operations, derive detector clusters or parity readouts from noisy circuits, reproduce the Q >= 60 proof, or establish schedule performance, a threshold, or fault tolerance.
next_gate: Implement the smallest deterministic gauging/ungauging lifecycle adapter that creates and terminates the measured D(Z3) region while preserving an explicit supplied fusion outcome; keep it independent of the noisy D4 extension.
